en: You must be the ones who came to hear the old tale of Lacunosa Town.
All right, my dears. Please sit and listen.
Wasn't that an interesting folktale? We can't say what the Pokémon was, but the power in the story is remarkable!
I know... A power that can freeze everything around it. It could rival the legendary dragons!
Yes, Bianca. It's rather like the dragons I told you of in Lentimas Town, who scorched Unova long ago.
Professor, do you think the Pokémon from the old story and the legendary dragons could be connected?
The dragons were woken from stones, the Light Stone and the Dark Stone. Suppose the meteorite in the tale and those stones were one and the same...
Remember that elements from the same age were found in the Dragonspiral Tower, where the dragons slept, and the pieces start to fit.
If your theory's right, it must be a really strong Pokémon. Why would it come out only at night, though? Maybe it doesn't like sunlight?
We'd have to look into it more deeply before I could say anything about that.
Now that I think of it, the name Lacunosa may come from lacunosus clouds, clouds that look like a net or a fence. I wonder whether the name is related.
Oh, sorry, I've rambled on, haven't I? {player}, could you ask Drayden about this, if you get the chance?
I'm going to do a little fieldwork. Bianca, you'll help me!
Oh, one more thing. Opelucid City's mayor, Drayden, wrestles with his Pokémon to make them tough. Don't be surprised!
Do you want to hear that old tale of Lacunosa Town again? It always takes me a little time to tell.
Oh, fine, fine. Come back when you have time.
